chunks: The day the trumpet is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills, and all will come to Him in humility.

key_terms.الصُّور: The Trumpet blown by the angel Israfil to signal the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.فَزِعَ: To be terrified or struck with awe/fear

ai.seo_question: What happens to all beings in the heavens and earth when the Trumpet is blown on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the universal awe of the Trumpet Blast (Nafkh al-Sur), with the exception of those Allah wills to spare often interpreted as the Ahl al-Bayt or the faithful who remain steadfast. It underscores the absolute submission (Dukhūr) of all creation, reinforcing the concept of Tawḥīd al-Afʿāl where every entity returns to Allah in humility, a theme central to the eschatological narratives in Nahj al-Balagha.
